Perfect! I've found the root cause. The pod events clearly show the issue. All 8 feature-backfill pods are stuck pending because the cluster-autoscaler is unable to scale up the nodes due to an AWS vCPU limit being exceeded.

Let me update the ticket with the findings:

input.note:
Root Cause: The cluster-autoscaler cannot provision new nodes for the feature-backfill pods due to an AWS vCPU limit being exceeded.

Evidence: All 8 feature-backfill pods are in Pending state with FailedScaleUp warnings showing: "VcpuLimitExceeded - You have requested more vCPU capacity than your current vCPU limit of 256 allows for the instance bucket that the specified instance type belongs to."

The pods request 12 vCPU each (8 pods = 96 vCPU total), but the AWS account has hit its vCPU limit for the c6i instance family. The cluster-autoscaler triggered a scale-up attempt but failed due to this limit.

Fix: Contact your AWS account team or the cloud platform team to request a vCPU limit increase for the c6i instance type family. AWS provides a limit increase request form at http://aws.amazon.com/contact-us/ec2-request. Once the vCPU limit is increased, the cluster-autoscaler will be able to provision the necessary nodes and your pods will start.
